dial.summary: DXY edged up to 100.60 (Sep 22 close) and real yields eased marginally to 2.63% (still near 18-year highs), keeping two structural macro headwinds in place; global M2 holding near $103.6T, the Fed balance sheet flat at $6.75T, BTC funding near-zero at 0.0095%, and stablecoin dominance declining to 10.25% sustain four supportive forces; with TOTAL rising toward ~$3.0T and BTC.D firm above 57%, the BTC Accumulation posture is maintained ahead of the data-dense September 30 triple-release (PCE, GDP, ADP) and October 2 NFP.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at ~$103.6T as of mid-September 2026 per MacroMicro/StreetStats (6–8 week reporting lag); US M2 reached $23.218T in July 2026 (+5.4% YoY) per MacroRadar — consistent with the G4 aggregate holding near $103.6T; global broad money supply (wider aggregate including all central banks) hit a record $150T in June 2026 (+$10.7T YoY) per spendnode.io; 4-week trend up confirmed (expansion from ~$103.0T in late August to $103.6T in mid-September, +0.6% over 4 weeks); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); no new G4 aggregate print yet for late September given the reporting lag.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1, below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down (Jul 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp); September ISM releases October 1 — no new data as of September 23; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); S&P Global US Flash PMI for September released today September 23 — the first advance read for September activity.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY closed at 100.603 on September 22, 2026 (rose 0.17% on the session per ChainCatcher; Trading Economics confirms ~100.42–100.60 range); dollar index at highest level in ~3 months, extending the prior week's +1.1% gain on hawkish Fed stance (fed funds 3.75%–4.00% post Sep 16 hike); 4-week trend up: ~99.0 (Aug 22) → 100.60 (Sep 22) = +1.6%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY holds above the 100 threshold; DXY above 100 joins real yields at 2.63% as the two active macro headwinds; a sustained official close below 100 is required to return to neutral status.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.63% as of September 21, 2026 per WatchGold/TradingView; breakeven inflation rate at 2.26%; Sep 21 10Y nominal at 4.96% minus 2.26% breakeven confirms real yield near 2.63–2.70% range; eased marginally from the Sep 18 peak of 2.66% (the highest 10Y TIPS level since October 2008 per TipsWatch); 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 22) → 2.63% (Sep 21) = +18bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); sustainably falling below 2% required to shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 21, 2026: 10Y at 4.96%, 2Y at 4.76%; spread = +0.20% (+20bps) per MacroMicro/YCharts; 4-week trend down (flattening): ~+38bps (Aug 21, pre-FOMC) → +20bps (Sep 21) = −18bps over 4 weeks, as the front end anchors to policy (fed funds 3.75%–4.00%) while the long end price-eases on growth moderation; status neutral (positive spread but not steepening; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); curve narrowed 2bps from the Sep 22 level of +22bps as 10Y eased; October 27–28 FOMC is the next key repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747B ($6.747T) for week ending September 16, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 (Treasuries $4,554B, MBS $1,914B, other $279B); next H.4.1 release scheduled September 24, 2026 (tomorrow); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.747T (Sep 16) = +$47B over 4 weeks, marginal expansion within the flat range; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilisation plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC; marginal expansion driven by FX swap line activity, not new asset purchases); total assets up ~$138B year-on-year.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.0095% per 8h as of September 22, 2026 per MacroMicro/TheBlock (30-day range: consistently sub-0.01% throughout September); near-zero funding during BTC's consolidation in the $84–87K range confirms the move remains spot-driven, not leveraged; 30-day trend flat (funding has remained sub-0.01% throughout September, no regime change); status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold; near-zero funding is the ideal BTC Accumulation signal; slight uptick from 0.008% to 0.0095% is within normal noise, not a trend shift).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$307B (September 22–23, 2026; StablecoinBeat/CoinGecko); total crypto market cap ~$3.0T (TOTAL rising modestly from $2.87T over the past week); stablecoin dominance 10.25% ($307B / ~$3.0T); 30-day trend down: stablecoin dominance peaked at ~13% in Q1 2026 and has declined to 10.25% by late September as capital has deployed into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; fell further from 10.66% on Sep 22 to 10.25% as TOTAL expanded; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply); BTC dominance firm above 57%; USDT ~60.57% ($183.4B), USDC ~24.1% ($74.2B); declining stablecoin dominance alongside firm BTC.D above 55% reinforces the BTC Accumulation thesis.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 19, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 19, 2026 — labor market read in the first full week post-FOMC/BOE/BOJ tightening cluster; a sustained rise above 220K would signal early labor market cracks under fed funds rate of 3.75%–4.00%; prior weeks approximately 206K; labor resilience is key to the FOMC's case for sustained restrictive policy heading into October 27–28; Fed balance sheet H.4.1 for week ending September 23 also releases tomorrow.

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Durable Goods Orders for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — watch non-defense capital goods ex-aircraft (key business investment proxy for Q3 GDP); elevated borrowing costs (10Y ~4.96%, real yields 2.63%) and DXY at 100.60 weigh on capex decisions; ISM Manufacturing new orders fell to 53.7 in August (−3.0pp); Q2 2026 GDP third estimate follows September 30.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Final)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers final September 2026 reading at 10:00 AM ET — first final sentiment read fully incorporating the post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) trifecta; year-ahead inflation expectations closely watched; a sharp drop in current conditions or spike in inflation expectations could shift November FOMC positioning; released same day as Advance Durable Goods.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — forward-looking consumer sentiment after September's global central bank tightening cluster; a sharp decline from August would confirm elevated financing costs (real yields 2.63%, 10Y ~4.96%) are weighing on consumer psychology; August PCE was +3.7% YoY; August PCE print follows the next day on September 30.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Labor Statistics Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — key Fed input for assessing labor market tightness; a significant decline toward 7M openings would signal elevated rates are cooling labor demand; October 27–28 FOMC will weigh this alongside September PCE (Sep 30) and September NFP (Oct 2).

upcoming.title: Q2 2026 GDP (Third Estimate)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Economic Analysis Q2 2026 GDP third (final) estimate at 8:30 AM ET — released alongside August PCE and ADP; a downward revision would add to recession concerns given the FOMC's hawkish Sep 16 hike and real yields at 2.63% (near 18-year high); includes BEA annual updates of national, industry, and regional data; a strong final print confirms the economy can absorb the current rate cycle despite tightening headwinds.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays report including August 2026 PCE Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; July 2026 PCE was +3.7% YoY; a reading above +3.5% YoY reinforces the FOMC's case for continued tightening ahead of October 27–28; core PCE (ex food and energy) watched most closely; released alongside Q2 GDP third estimate and ADP; the last major inflation print before the October FOMC blackout period.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP Research Institute private payrolls estimate for September 2026 at 8:15 AM ET — advance read on labor conditions ahead of official NFP (Oct 2); released alongside Q2 GDP and August PCE on a data-dense final day of September; a strong print (+150K or above) reinforces the NFP-resilient narrative and keeps rate-hike expectations elevated for the October 27–28 FOMC.
